subject: Astronomy & Space
title: Europa: Ocean Under Ice
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Europa: Ocean Under Ice.

hook.text: Jupiter's moon Europa has a global ocean of liquid water under a shell of ice. It may be the best place to find alien life.

buildup.text: The ocean is kept liquid by tidal heating—Jupiter's gravity flexes Europa, generating internal warmth.

discovery.text: Hubble detected water plumes erupting from Europa's surface. A future probe could fly through them and taste the ocean.

twist.text: Europa's ocean floor may have hydrothermal vents—the same environment where life may have originated on Earth.

climax.text: NASA's Europa Clipper launched in 2024 to study the moon's ice shell, ocean, and chemistry up close.

punchline.text: An ocean twice the volume of Earth's. Hidden under ice. We're finally going to look.

quiz.question: What keeps Europa's ocean liquid despite being so far from the Sun?
options: Tidal heating from Jupiter's gravitational pull flexes the moon and generates warmth
Radioactive decay in Europa's core provides all the heat needed
The ice shell traps solar radiation and creates a greenhouse effect

details.summary: Jupiter's moon Europa hides a liquid saltwater ocean beneath a kilometers-thick ice shell, containing roughly twice the water of all Earth's oceans. Tidal heating from Jupiter's gravity keeps the ocean liquid, and interaction between water and a rocky seafloor could provide the chemistry life needs.
details.whyItMatters: Europa is considered one of the most promising places to find present-day extraterrestrial life. Its ocean has water, energy from tidal heating, and potentially the chemical nutrients needed for biology.
takeaways: Europa has a saltwater ocean twice the volume of Earth's oceans
Tidal heating from Jupiter keeps the ocean liquid
Water-rock interaction may provide chemistry for life

faq.question: How thick is Europa's ice shell?
faq.answer: Estimates range from 10 to 30 kilometers. The ice shell shows fractures and chaotic terrain suggesting it moves and cracks, possibly allowing ocean material to reach the surface. Some models predict thin spots where the ocean is only a few kilometers below.

faq.question: Could there be hydrothermal vents on Europa's seafloor?
faq.answer: Tidal heating likely warms Europa's rocky interior, making seafloor hydrothermal vents probable. On Earth, hydrothermal vents support thriving ecosystems independent of sunlight. If Europa has similar vents, they could provide the energy and chemicals that life requires.
